question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹49, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1st year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 49 − 42 = ₹7

Rate of interest (R) = (Difference ÷ SI for 1st year) × 100 = (7 ÷ 21) × 100 = 100/3%

Principal = (SI for 1st year × 100) ÷ R = (21 × 100) ÷ (100/3) = 21 × 3 = ₹63

**∴ The correct answer is ₹63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SI for 2 years = ₹42

CI for 2 years = ₹49

**Formula Used:**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P(R/100)²

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = 49 − 42 = ₹7

⇒ In Compound Interest, the extra amount earned in the 2nd year is the interest on the 1st year's Simple Interest.

⇒ Rate (R) = (7 ÷ 21) × 100 = 100/3%

⇒ Substituting R into the difference formula: CI − SI = P(R/100)²

⇒ 7 = P × (100 ÷ 300)²

⇒ 7 = P × (1/3)²

⇒ 7 = P × (1/9)

⇒ P = 7 × 9 = 63

**∴ The correct answer is ₹63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of exactly two years is given by the formula: Diff = P(R/100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

For a period of exactly three years, the difference formula extends to: Diff = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compound vs Simple Interest Mechanics

For the first year (when compounded annually), the Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always identical. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest generates an extra value which is simply the "Interest computed on the accumulated Interest" from the previous years.
